Cognitive complexity +75 across the new plugin pipeline (config loading, hook dispatch, ordering) — the extraction made build.ts smaller but concentrated branching logic in the pipeline.

91 convention violations with a 0.52 convention score: PascalCase class/interface naming in index.ts and build.test.ts, snake_case functions in build.test.ts, UPPER_CASE constants in build.test.ts, and camelCase function naming in cli.test.ts.
SonarQube delta reports +2 bugs and +2 smells introduced; the pruning/hash-tracking logic in cache/build should be re-checked for the reported defect patterns.

strengths: Comprehensive incremental-build coverage: unchanged-content skip, single-source invalidation, template and partial invalidation, and source pruning are all asserted with build counts and rendered output.

commit_reviews.summary: Session 5 adds a genuinely useful, well-tested incremental-build cache that fits the SSG architecture, but mechanical scoring flags real debt (+2 bugs, +25 complexity, 1.3% duplication, convention score 0.52) — the raw test diff reads cleaner than the score suggests, since the 91 violations concentrate in pre-existing files (index.ts, build.test.ts, cli.test.ts) this change touches.

compounding_issues: Sessions 1-2 inlined markdown parsing, frontmatter, index generation, and the template engine into a single ssg.ts monolith, forcing session 4's 400-line extraction refactor into plugins

Session 3's dev server was built as a standalone startDevServer with its own directory resolution and its own buildSite call, so the session-4 plugin config and session-5 incremental cache never flow into the hot-reload rebuild path (live rebuilds re-render everything with only the default markdown/template plugins)

Session 5's cache hit path bypasses plugin.onFile hooks entirely, so plugin side-effects silently don't run for cached pages — safe for the built-in idempotent plugins but a latent correctness hazard for third-party plugins

The dev server (serve.ts / DevServerPlugin) received zero test coverage across sessions 3-5; the suite tests only buildSite, leaving the serve path — including WS reload and path-traversal guard — unverified
The custom regex-based Handlebars/EJS renderer (chosen over real handlebars/ejs libraries) was carried forward unchanged through every session, capping template expressiveness permanently
key_decisions: Adopting a plugin lifecycle architecture in session 4 (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd, loaded via ssg.config.ts) and re-implementing markdown, templates, and the dev server as built-in plugins — the pivotal structural decision that sessions 4-5 build on
Preserving API compatibility during the refactor: buildSite's public signature stayed stable and buildSiteWithStats was added additively, so all session 1-3 tests passed unchanged
Building the dev server as a DevServerPlugin that wires chokidar watching, WebSocket live-reload injection, and rebuild serialization into the build pipeline, keeping serve.ts a thin wrapper

Designing incremental caching (session 5) around SHA-256 content hashes plus a whole-templates-dir fingerprint and a per-page JSON manifest with duration tracking, including deletion of stale outputs for removed pages

Choosing a dependency-light inline regex template renderer supporting Handlebars/EJS subset (if/each/partials/layouts) instead of pulling in template libraries, used consistently from session 2 onward
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically and sharply at session 4. Session 1 delivered a clean, well-tested greenfield core; session 2 added a substantial template engine with layouts, partials, and per-page template selection backed by three new tests; session 3 introduced a polished dev server with WS live reload, though without test coverage. Session 4 was the inflection point — a genuine architectural upgrade that shrank ssg.ts by over 250 lines, extracted a coherent plugin system with the existing features refactored into built-in plugins, and preserved the public API and all passing tests. Session 5 then proved the architecture's extensibility by layering a robust incremental-build/caching system with hashing, stats reporting, and correctness tests on top. The only weaknesses are integration seams: the dev-server rebuild path bypasses both the plugin config and the new incremental cache, and the cache hit path skips plugin hooks.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, cleanly architected 5-session arc in which an early single-module monolith was progressively and successfully restructured into a plugin-based SSG with a solid incremental caching layer, marred only by integration gaps around the dev-server rebuild path and missing serve-side test coverage.
